html:
Castillo San Felipe del Morro is the fortress at the entrance to San Juan Bay in Puerto Rico, begun by the Spanish in 1539 and enlarged over two centuries. It guarded the gateway of the treasure fleets to the Caribbean.

It drove off Francis Drake in 1595. The English under the Earl of Cumberland took the city by land in 1598, and the Dutch burned it in 1625, but El Morro held. The British attacked again in 1797 and were repelled.

With San Cristobal and the walls of Old San Juan, it is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site. US warships shelled it in the Spanish-American War of 1898, and it served as a US Army post until 1961. It is now a symbol of Puerto Rico.
